description:
## Finding
\`pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:74-82\` and \`pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:38-43\` document this directly:
> Both the base CRL and the delta CRL (if present) are re-parsed from DER on every \`check_revocation\` call.
> The OCSP response is re-parsed from DER on every \`check_revocation\` call.

Both note tracking for v0.3.

## Why P3
- Documented limitation, not a defect.
- For a chain of N=5 certs against the same CRL, this is 5x redundant parse work.
- Practically not large for typical CRLs (KB-MB) but would matter for very large enterprise CRLs.

## Fix
Cache the parsed structure inside \`CrlChecker\` / \`OcspChecker\`. Two implementation options:
1. Parse eagerly in \`new\` / \`with_delta\`, store the parsed value; signature is verified on first \`check_revocation\` and cached.
2. Use \`OnceCell\`-style lazy parse on first call.

Option 1 is simpler and surfaces parse errors at construction (better UX). Both eliminate the redundant work.

## Scope reference
\`pkix-revocation/src/crl.rs:79-82\` (limitation note), \`208\` (\`check_revocation\` body), \`357\` (\`check_revocation_against_anchor\`); \`pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs:38-43,93,219\`.
title: P3: pkix-revocation re-parses CRL/OCSP DER on every check_revocation call
